ιαινω.g: ἰαίνω , aor. ιηνα, pass. ιάνθη (ῖ when with augment): warm, soften by warming, Od. 12.175; met., warm, melt, move the heart to compassion, cheer, etc., Od. 15.379; often thus in pass., θυ_μός, κῆρ, Il. 23.598, Od. 22.59; μέτωπον ἰάνθη, ‘brightened,’ Il. 15.103; also w. acc. of specification, θυ_μόν, φρένας, ψ 47, Od. 24.382; w. dat., Od. 19.537.

ιαλλω.g: ἰάλλω , aor. ἴηλα, inf. ἰῆλαι: send, mostly implying quick motion toward some definite point; freq. ἐπ᾽ ὀνείατα χεῖρας ἰάλλειν, ‘apply’ the hands to viands, Il. 9.91, etc.; ἑτάροις ἐπὶ (adv.) χεῖρας ἴαλλεν, ‘flung out’ his arms to them, Od. 9.288 ; ὀιστὸν ἀπὸ νευρῆφιν ἴαλλεν | Ἕκτορος ἀντικρυ?, Il. 8.300; ἐπὶ (adv.) δεσμὸν ἴηλον, ‘whip’ on a knot, Od. 8.443, cf. 497; met., ἀτι_μίῃσιν ἰάλλειν, ‘assail’ as with missiles, Od. 13.142.

ιαλμενοσ.g: Ἰάλμενος : a son of Ares, leader of Boeotians, Il. 2.512, Il. 9.82.

ιαομαι.g: ίάομαι , ipf. ίᾶτο, fut. ι?ήσεται, aor. ίηοάμην: heal, cure, Il. 12.2, Od. 9.525.

ιαπτω.g: ἰάπτω : only μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ (adv.) χρόα κα_λὸν ἰάπτῃ（ς), harm by smiting, Od. 2.376, Od. 4.749.

ιαρδανοσ.g: Ἰάρδανος : the river Iardanus.— (1) in Crete, Od. 3.292.—(2) in Elis, near Pheiae, Il. 7.135.

ιασιδησ.g: Ἰασίδης : son of Iasus.—(1) Amphīon, Od. 11.283.—(2) Dmetor, Od. 17.443.

ιασιων.g: Ἰασίων : a mortal beloved by Demeter, and slain by the thunderbolt of Zeus, Od. 5.125†.

ιασον.g: Ἴασον Ἄργος: Iasian Argos, meaning the whole of the Peloponnēsus, the origin of the epithet being unknown, Od. 18.246†.

ιασοσ.g: Ἴασος : (1) son of Sphelus, a leader of the Athenians, slain by Aenēas, Il. 15.332.—(2) the father of Amphīon.— (3) the father of Dmetor.

ιαυω.g: ἰαύω (cf. ἄϝεσα), ipf. ἴαυον, iter. ἰαύεσκον, aor. inf. ἰαῦσαι: sleep, rest, lie; πολλάς μὲν ἀύπνους νύκτας ἴαυον, Il. 9.325, 470, Od. 19.340.

ιαχη.g: ἰαχή (ϝιαχή): loud, sharp cry, shriek; of men in battle, Il. 4.456; the shades in the nether world, Od. 11.43; hunters, Il. 15.275.

ιαχω.g: ἰάχω (ϝιάχω), ipf. ιαχον (ῖ when with augment): cry loud and sharply, shriek, scream; of applause, the cry of battle, of wounded men, Il. 23.766, Il. 4.506, Il. 5.343, etc.; of Circe, threatened with Odysseus's sword, Od. 10.323; of a child, Il. 6.468; transferred to inanimate objects, the ‘twanging’ of the bow-string, Il. 4.125; the ‘blare’ of the trumpet, Il. 18.219; ‘hissing’ of hot iron in water, Od. 9.392; ‘crackling’ of fire, Il. 23.216; but the Eng. words do not involve a personification like the Greek.

ιαωλκοσ.g: Ἰαωλκός : Iolcus, a town in Thessaly on the Pagasaean gulf, Od. 11.256, Il. 2.712.

ιγνυη.g: ἰγνύη (γόνυ): hollow of the knee, Il. 13.212†.

ιδαιοσ.g: Ἰδαῖος : of Mt. Ida, Idaean, epith. of the mountains belonging to the range, Il. 8.170, Il. 20.189; also of Zeus, whose grove and altar were upon Gargaron, Il. 16.605, Il. 24.291.

ιδη.g: Ἴδη : Ida, a mountain range, rich in springs, ravines, forest, and game, extending from Phrygia, through Mysia, toward the Hellespont, and subsiding into the plain near Troy, Il. 2.821, Il. 11.183; its summit, Γάργαρον.—?῎ιδηθεν, from Ida.

ιδησ.g: Ἴδης : a famous archer, the father of Cleopatra, Il. 9.558†.

ιδιοσ.g: ἴδιος : private, opp. δήμιος, Od. 3.82 and Od. 4.314.

ιδνοω.g: ἰδνόω , pass. aor. ἰδνώθη, part. -θείς: bend back ward, double up, pass. as mid., Il. 2.266, Od. 8.375.

ιδομενευσ.g: Ἰδομενεύς : Idomeneus, son of Deucalion, grandson of Minos, king in Crete, Il. 4.265, Il. 12.117, Il. 2.645; his son Arsilochus, Od. 13.259; comrade-at-arms, Meriones, Il. 23.113.

ιδρισ.g: ἴδρις (ϝιδρ.): knowing, skilled, skilful. w. inf., Od. 7.108. (Od.)

ιδροω.g: ἱδρόω (ἱδρώς), part. ἱδρώοντα, etc., fem. pl. ἱδρῶσαι, fut. ἱδρώσει, aor. ἵδρωσα: sweat.

ιδρυω.g: ἱδρύω (root ἑδ), aor. ἵδρυ_σα, pass. ἱδρύνθην: cause or bid to be seated, Il. 2.191; pass., take seats, be seated, Il. 3.78.

ιενται, ιεσθε.g: ἴενται, ἴεσθε : more correct reading, ἵενται, ἵεσθε, see ἵημι.

ιερευσ, ιρευσ.g: ἱερεύς, ίρεύς , ῆος: priest, in charge of the sacrifices to some special god, also soothsayer, Il. 11.23.

ιερευω, ιρευω.g: ἱερεύω, ίρεύω , ipf. iter. ίρεύεσκον, fut. inf. ἱερεύσειν, aor. ἱέρευσα, pass. plup. ἱέρευτο, mid. aor. inf. ίρεύσασθαι: sacrifice, esp. by killing the victim, offer, then, in general, slaughter, Il. 6.174 ; ξείνῳ, ‘in honor of the guest,’ Od. 14.414; mid., subjective, Od. 19.198.

ιερηιον.g: ἱερηιον : victim, animal for sacrifice or slaughter, Od. 14.94.

ιερον, ιρον.g: ἱερόν, ίρόν , neut. of ἱερός as subst.: sacrifice, victim, Od. 1.61, Il. 1.147.

ιεροσ, ιροσ.g: ιερός, ίρός : (1) strong, powerful; ίς, μένος, φυλάκων τέλος, πυλαωροί, στρατός, Od. 2.409, Od. 7.167, Il. 10.56, Il. 24.681, Od. 24.81; ἰχθύς, ‘lively,’ Il. 16.407.—(2) sacred, hallowed.

ιζανω.g: ἱζάνω (ἵζω): sit; trans., cause or bid to be seated, Il. 23.258.

ιζω.g: ἵζω (root ἑδ), ipf. ἷζον, iter. ἵζεσκε: take a seat, sit down, sit still, rest; βουλήν, ‘hold a council,’ ‘session,’ Il. 2.53; mid., like act., of an ambuscade, Il. 18.522.

ιηλυ_σοσ.g: Ἰηλυ_σός : a town in Rhodes, Il. 2.656†.

ιημι.g: ἵημι , ἵησι, 3 pl. ἱεῖσι, inf. ιέμεναι, part. ἱέντες, ιεῖσαι, imp. ἵει, ipf. ἵει, 3 pl. ἵεν, fut. ἥσω, aor. ἧκα, ἕηκα, 3 pl. ἧκαν and ἕσαν, subj. ᾗσιν, opt. εἵην, inf. εἷναι, mid. pres. ἵεται, imp. ἵεσθε, part. ιεμενος, ipf. ίετο, ἵεντο, aor. 3 pl. ἕντο: let go, i. e. set in motion of any sort.—I. act., send, ἄγγελόν τινι, Il. 18.182; put to anything, as harness, Il. 16.152; throw, let fly, μετὰ (adv.) δ᾽ ίὸν ἕηκεν, ‘in among them,’ Il. 1.48; so ‘let fall’ anything, as tears, a sword from the hand, ‘let down’ the hair, ‘let on’ water, Il. 12.25, and of the river itself ‘rolling’ its waters (thus, intrans., Od. 11.239, Od. 7.130); metaph., of ‘dismissing,’ i. e. by satisfying, a desire, ἔρον, Il. 13.638; ‘inspiring’ one with force, Il. 5.125; ‘laying’ misfortune on one, Il. 10.71. The applications of the word are very numerous, but always distinct if the fundamental signification be held in mind. The ground-meaning, as may be seen from the examples, usually gets a specific turn from the context, esp. by means of adverbs (ἐν, ἐξ, κατά, μετά, etc.).—II. mid., set oneself in motion at something (τινός), ἱέμενος ποταμοῖο ῥοάων, ‘giving thyself a direction’ toward Oceanus, Od. 10.529; so ‘press on,’ ‘hasten,’ Il. 13.707, Il. 12.274; met., with and without θυ_μῷ, ‘strive after’ (τινός), ‘be eager,’ Il. 23.371 ; θυ_μός, Il. 8.301; freq. phrase, ἐπεὶ πόσιος καὶ ἐδητύος ἐξ ἔρον ἕντο, had dismissed ‘from themselves,’ Il. 1.469, Od. 1.150.

ιησονιδησ.g: Ἰησονίδης : son of Iēson (Jason), Euneus, Il. 7.468, 471, Il. 23.747.

ιησων.g: Ἰήσων : Iēson (Jason), the leader of the Argonauts, Od. 12.72

ιητροσ.g: ίητρός (ἰάομαι): healer, surgeon, physician; with ἀνήρ, Il. 11.514.

ιθαι - γενησ.g: ἰθαι - γένης (ἰθύς): born in lawful wedlock, legitimate, Od. 14.203†.

ιθακη.g: Ἰθάκη : Ithaca.—(1) the native island of Odysseus, with Mts. Neritus, Neius, and Corax, and the harbor Reithrum. Epithets, ἀμφίαλος, εὐδείελος, ἐυκτιμένη, κραναή, παιπαλόεσσα, τρηχεῖα.—(2) the city, at the foot of Mt. Neius, Od. 3.81, cf. Od. 16.322 .—Ἰθάκηνδε, to Ithaca.—Ἰθακήσιος: inhabitant of Ithaca, Ithacan.

ιθακοσ.g: Ἴθακος : the eponymous hero of the island of Ithaca, Od. 17.207†.

ιθι.g: ἴθι , imp. of εἶμι: come! go! employed as an interjection, freq. with ἄγε.

ιθμα.g: ἴθμα , ατος: step, gait, pl., Il. 5.778†.

ιθυνω.g: ίθύνω (ἰθύς), aor. ίθυ_να, subj. ἰθύνομεν. make straight, straighten, ἐπὶ στάθμην, ‘to the line,’ Od. 5.245; pass., ἵππω δ᾽ ἰθυ_νθήτην, ‘placed themselves in line’ with the pole of the chariot, Il. 16.475; guide a ship, chariot, etc., and, of missiles, aim, direct, Il. 5.290, Il. 17.632, mid., ‘his arrow,’ Od. 22.8.

ιθυσ.g: ίθύς , εῖα, ύ: straight; τέτραπτο πρὸς ἰθύ οἱ, ‘straight opposite him,’ Il. 14.403; usually metaph., straight, right, just, Il. 23.580; sup., ἰθύντατα, most fairly, Il. 18.508.—As adv., ίθύς, ι᾿θύ, straight at, straight for, τινός, Il. 5.849; also with prepositions, and abs., Il. 20.99, Od. 3.10 ; ίθὺς φέρειν, μάχεσθαι, φρονεῖν, ‘turn the mind straight on,’ ‘be bent on battle,’ Il. 13.135, cf. Il. 11.95.

ιθυω.g: ίθύω , aor. ίθυ_σα: go straight forward, advance, attack, of warriors, a lion, Il. 12.48; w. gen., νεός, Il. 15.693; w. inf., ‘strive,’ Od. 11.591.

ιθωμη.g: Ἰθώμη : a town in Thessaly, Il. 2.729†.

ικανω.g: ἱκάνω (ίκω), mid. ἱκάνομαι: come to, arrive at, reach, w. acc. of person or thing attained to, less often with prep., Il. 1.431; freq. of supplication, γούναθ᾽ ἱκάνω, Od. 5.449; met., ‘come upon,’ ‘come home to,’ ὕπνος, θέσφατα, Κ 96, Od. 9.507, etc. Often with perf. signif., ‘am come to,’ Il. 9.197, Od. 6.119.

ικαριοσ.g: Ἰκάριος : Icarius, the brother of Tyndareus, and father of Penelope, Od. 1.276, 329, Od. 4.797.

ικετα_ονιδησ.g: Ἱκετα_ονίδης : son of Hicetāon, Melanippus, Il. 15.546†.

ικεταων.g: Ἱκετάων : (1) a son of Laomedon, and brother of Priam, Il. 3.147, Il. 20.238.— (2) the father of Melanippus, Il. 15.576.

ικετευω.g: ἱκετεύω (ἱκέτης), aor. ἱκέτευσα: ap- proach as suppliant, supplicate, τινά, also w. praep. (Od. and Il. 16.574).

ικετησ.g: ἱκέτης (ίκω): suppliant, for protection of any sort, but esp. one in search of purification from homicide (cf. Tlepolemus, Lycophron, Patroclus), Od. 9.269, Il. 21.75.

ικετησιοσ.g: ἱκετήσιος : of suppliants, protector of suppliants, epith. of Zeus, Od. 13.213†.

ικμαλιοσ.g: Ἰκμάλιος : a joiner in Ithaca, Od. 19.57†.

ικμενοσ.g: ἴκμενος : fair wind (οὖρος), a wind ‘that follows fast’ (secundus). (Od.)

ικνεομαι.g: ἱκνέομαι (ἵκω), part. ἱκνεύμεναι, ipf. ἱκνεύμεσθα, fut. ἵξομαι, aor. ικόμην, 2 sing. ικευ (ῖ when with augment): come to, arrive at, reach, w. acc., also with praep.; ‘return,’ when the context gives this sense, Od. 23.151; esp. ‘approach as suppliant,’ ‘supplicate,’ Il. 14.260, Il. 22.123, Od. 9.267; met., ποθή, κάματος, σέβας, τί σε φρένας ίκετο πένθος; Il. 1.362.

ικρια.g: ἴκρια , ἰκριόφιν, pl.: deck-beams, deck, which in the Homeric ship was partial, only fore and aft (see plate IV., at end of volume); also ribs of a ship. (See cut No. 32.)

ικω.g: ίκω , subj. ίκωμι, ipf. ἷκε, aor. ἷξον: come (to), reach; ἵκω is the stem-form answering to ἱκάνω and ἱκνέομαι, and has the same applications and constructions as those verbs; πινυτὴ φρένας ίκει, ‘informs,’ Od. 20.228.

ιλα_οσ.g: ἵλα_ος : appeased, hence propitious, gracious, kind. (Il.)

ιλασκομαι.g: ίλάσκομαι and ίλάομαι (Il. 2.550), ipf. ίλάσκοντο, aor. subj. (or fut.) ίλάσσομαι, ίλασόμεσθα, part. ίλασσάμενοι: reconcile to oneself, appease, propitiate.

ιληιοσ.g: Ἰλήιος (ϝῖλ.): of Ilus, πεδίον, so named, according to the scholiast, from the tomb of Ilus, Il. 21.558†.

ιλημι.g: ίλημι , imp. ἵληθι, perf. subj. ίλήκησι, opt. ίλήκοι; be propitious, gracious, Od. 3.380. (Od.)

ιλιοθι.g: Ἰλιόθι (ϝῖλ.): always with πρό, before Ilium.

ιλιοσ.g: Ἴλιος (ϝίλιος) and ?῎ιλιον (Il. 15.71): Ilium, a name for Troy derived from that of its founder Ilus; epithets, αἰπεινή, αἰπύ, ἐρατεινή, εὐτείχεος, ἠνεμόεσσα, ἱερή, ὀφρυόεσσα. In wider signification, for the region about Troy, Il. 1.71, Od. 19.182. In Il. 15.66, Il. 21.104, Il. 22.6, the true form of the gen. is Ἰλίοο, as the scansion shows (cf. Αἴολος).

ιλλασ.g: ἰλλάς , άδος (εἴλω): pl., twisted cords, Il. 13.572†.

ιλοσ.g: Ἶλος : Ilus.—(1) son of Tros, and father of Laomedon, Il. 11.166, Il. 20.232; his tomb, Il. 10.415, Il. 11.372.—(2) son of Mermeros of Ephyra, Od. 1.259.

ιμασ.g: ιμάς , αντος: leather strap or thong. —(1) in connection with the chariot, (a) straps in which the chariot - box was hung, or perhaps more likely the network of plaited straps enclosing the body of the chariot, Il. 5.727; (b) the reins, Il. 23.324, 363; (c) the halter, Il. 8.544.—(2) the chin-strap of a helmet, Il. 3.371.—(3) the cestus of boxers, see πυγμάχοι.—(4) the leash or latchstring by which doors were fastened. See adjacent cut, in four divisions: above, the closed, below the unfastened door; on the left, as seen from the inner side, on the right as seen from the outside. To close the door from the outside, the string, hanging loosely in fig. 1, was pulled until it drew the bolt from the position of fig. 2 to that of fig. 3, when it was made fast by a knot to the ring, κορώνη, e, fig. 4. To open from the outside, the string was first untied, and then the κληίς, not unlike a hook (fig. 4, f), was introduced through the key-hole, c, and by means of a crook (g, fig. 3) at the end of it the bolt was pushed back from the position of fig. 3 to that of fig. 2, and the door opened, Od. 1.442.— (5) for a bed - cord, Od. 23.201.—(6) the magic girdle of Aphrodīte, Il. 14.214, 219. —(7) a thong to make a drill revolve, Od. 9.385. (See cut No. 121.)

ιμασσω.g: ἱμάσσω , aor. ἵμασε, subj. ἱμάσσω: lash, scourge, beat, Il. 5.589, Il. 2.782, Il. 15.17.

ιμβρασιδησ.g: Ἰμβρασίδης : son of Imbrasus, Piroüs, Il. 4.520†.

ιμβριοσ.g: Ἴμβριος : (1) inhabitant of Imbros, Imbrian, Il. 21.43.—(2) the son of Mentor, son-in-law of Priam, slain by Teucer, Il. 13.171, 197.

ιμβροσ.g: Ἴμβρος : Imbros, an island on the coast of Thrace, with capital city of the same name, Il. 14.281, Il. 13.33.

ιμειρω.g: ίμείρω (ίμερος), mid. ίμείρεται, ἱμειρόμενος, aor. opt. ίμείραιτο, subj. ίμείρεται: long for, yearn for, τινός, and w. inf., Od. 10.431, Il. 14.163.

ιμεροεισ.g: ίμερόεις , εσσα, εν (ίμερος): passionate, fond, lovely; γόος, ἔργα γάμοιο, ἀοιδή, Od. 10.398, Ε 429, Od. 1.421.—Adv., ίμερόεν κιθάριζε, charmingly, Il. 18.570.

ιμεροσ.g: ίμερος : longing, passion, love; freq, w. obj. gen.; w. two genitives, πατρὸς ίμερος γόοιο, ‘yearning after tears, to weep for his father,’ Il. 24.507, Od. 4.113.

ινα.g: ἵνα : (1) adv., where; this meaning being the primary one, is to be assumed in preference to signif. (2), when the sense admits, e. g. Il. 24.382. Apparently demonstrative, there, in Il. 10.127.—(2) conj., in order that, that; rarely with κέ, Od. 12.156.

ινδαλλομαι.g: ἰνδάλλομαι (root ϝιδ): be seen, appear, w. part., Il. 17.213 ; ὥς μοι ἰνδάλλεται ἦτορ, impers., ‘as floats before me in recollection’ (ἦτορ like κατὰ θυ_μόν), Od. 19.224.

ινιον.g: ίνίον (ϝῖν.): bone of the back of the head. (Il.)

ιξαλοσ.g: ἴξαλος : doubtful word, spry, epith. of the wild goat, Il. 4.105†.

ιξι_ονιοσ.g: Ἰξι_όνιος : ἄλοχος Ἰξι_ονίη, wife of Ixīon, Il. 14.317†.

ιο-δνεφησ.g: ἰο-δνεφής , ές (ϝίον, δνόφος): violetdark, dark-hued, εἶρος. (Od.)

ιο - ειδησ.g: ἰο - ειδής , ές (ϝίον, ϝεῖδος): violetcolored, deep blue, epith. of the sea.

ιοεισ.g: ἰόεις , εσσα (ϝίον) = ἰοειδής, of iron, Il. 23.850†.

ιο-μωροσ.g: ἰό-μωρος (ϝιομ.): doubtful word, a disparaging epithet applied to the Greeks, Ἀργεῖοι ἰόμωροι, boasters. (Il.)

ιοτησ.g: ἰότης , ητος: will, mostly θεῶν ἰότητι, Od. 7.214, etc.; μνηστήρων ἰότητι, ‘according to their wish,’ Od. 18.234.

ιουλοσ.g: ἴουλος (οὖλος): first growth of beard, down, Od. 11.319†.

ιο-χεαιρα.g: ίο-χέαιρα (χέω): pouring arrows, αρξηερεσς, epith. of Artemis, both as adj. and subst.

ιππασιδησ.g: Ἱππασίδης : son of Hippasus.—(1) Apisāon, Il. 17.348.—(2) Hypsēnor, Il. 13.411.—(3) Charops, Il. 11.426.—(4) Socus, Il. 11.431.

ιππειοσ.g: ἵππειος : of horses, horse-; λόφος, horse-hair plume.

ιππευσ.g: ἱππεύς , ῆος, pl. ἱππῆες: chariotman, whether as warrior fighting from the chariot, or as competitor in a chariot-race, Il. 4.297, Il. 23.262.

ιππ-ηλασιοσ.g: ἱππ-ηλάσιος (ἐλαύνω): for driving chariots; ἱππηλασίη ὁδός, Il. 7.340 and 439.

ιππ - ηλατα.g: ἱππ - ηλάτα (ἐλαύνω), for -άτης: driver of steeds, chariot-fighter, knight.

ιππ-ηλατοσ.g: ἱππ-ήλατος : passable with chariots, adapted to driving horses. (Od.)

ιππ-ημολγοι.g: Ἱππ-ημολγοί (ἀμέλγω): the Hippemolgi, ‘mare-milkers,’ a Scythian tribe, Il. 13.5.

ιππιο - χαιτησ.g: ἱππιο - χαίτης (χαίτη): of horsehair; λόφος, Il. 6.469†.

ιππιο-χαρμησ.g: ἱππιο-χάρμης (χάρμη): fighter from a chariot, Il. 24.257, Od. 11.259.

ιππο-βοτοσ.g: ἱππό-βοτος (βόσκω): horse-nourishing, horse - breeding, esp. as epith. of Argos, Il. 2.287.

ιπποδαμα_σ.g: Ἱπποδάμα_ς : a Trojan, slain by Achilles, Il. 20.401.

ιπποδαμεια.g: Ἱπποδάμεια : Hippodamīa.—(1) a daughter of Anchīses, Il. 13.429.—(2) an attendant of Penelope, Od. 18.182.—(3) the wife of Pirithoüs, Il. 2.742.

ιππο - δαμοσ.g: ἱππό - δαμος (δαμάζω): horse-taming, epith. of the Trojans, and of individual heroes. (Il. and Od. 3.17, 181.)

ιπποδαμοσ.g: Ἱππόδαμος : a Trojan, slain by Odysseus, Il. 11.335†.

ιππο-δασεια.g: ἱππο-δάσεια (δασύς, εῖα): with thick horse-hair plume, epith. of the helmet. (Il. and Od. 22.111, 145.)

ιπποθεν.g: ἱππόθεν : from the (wooden) horse, Od. 8.515, Od. 11.531.

ιπποθοοσ.g: Ἱππόθοος : (1) a son of Priam, Il. 24.251.—(2) a leader of the Pelasgians, slain by Ajax, Il. 17.289.

ιππο - κελευθοσ.g: ἱππο - κέλευθος : making way with the chariot, swift-driving, epith. of Patroclus. (Il.)

ιππο-κορυστησ.g: ἱππο-κορυστής (κορύσσω): chariotequipped, chariot-fighter, epith. of the Maeonians and Paeonians, and of individual heroes, Il. 2.1, Il. 24.677.

ιπποκοων.g: Ἱπποκόων : a cousin of Rhesus, Il. 10.518†.

ιππολοχοσ.g: Ἱππόλοχος : (1) son of Antimachus, slain by Agamemnon, Il. 11.122.— (2) a Lycian, son of Bellerophon, the father of Glaucus, Il. 6.206.

ιππο - μαχοσ.g: ἱππό - μαχος : fighting from horses (chariots), Il. 10.431†.

ιππομαχοσ.g: Ἱππόμαχος : a Trojan, the son of Antimachus, slain by Leonteus, Il. 12.189†.

ιππονοοσ.g: Ἱππόνοος : a Greek, slain by Hector, Il. 11.303†.

ιππο-πολοσ.g: ἱππό-πολος (πολεύω): horse-managing, horse-training, Thracians, Il. 13.4 and Il. 14.227.

ιπποσ.g: ἵππος : horse or mare; ἄρσενες ἵπποι, ‘stallions,’ Od. 13.81 ; θήλεες ἵπποι, ἵπποι θήλειαι, Ε 269, Il. 11.681; the Homeric Greeks did not ride horseback, but employed chariots; hence ἵπποι, oftener ἵππω, span, chariot, alone or w. ἅρμα, Il. 12.120; freq. ἵπποισιν καὶ ὄχεσφιν, Il. 12.114, 119; ἐξ or ἀφ᾽ ἵππων ἀποβῆναι, Γ 265, Il. 5.13; of chariotmen as opposed to infantry, Od. 14.267, Il. 2.554, Il. 16.167, Il. 18.153.

ιπποσυνη.g: ἱπποσύνη : horsemanship, i. e. chariot-fighting. (Il. and Od. 24.40.)

ιπποτα.g: ἱππότα , for -ότης: horseman, knight, esp. as epith. of Nestor, Il. 2.336, 628.

ιπποταδησ.g: Ἱπποτάδης : son of Hippotes, Aeolus, Il. 10.36†.

ιπποτιων.g: Ἱπποτίων : an Ascanian, slain by Meriones, Il. 13.792, Il. 14.514.

ιππ-ουρισ.g: ἵππ-ουρις , ιος (οὐρα?): with horsetail plume, epith. of the helmet. (Il. and Od. 22.124.)

ιπτομαι.g: ἴπτομαι , fut. ἴψεται, aor. 2 sing. ἴψαο: smite, chastise, afflict; said of gods and kings, Il. 1.454, Il. 2.193.

ιρη.g: Ἱρή : a town in Messēne, under the sway of Agamemnon, Il. 9.150, 292.

ιρηξ.g: ίρηξ , ηκος: hawk or falcon; typical of swiftness, Il. 15.237.

ιρισ.g: ἶρις (ϝῖρις), dat. pl. ίρισσιν: rainbow, Il. 11.27, Il. 17.547.—Personified, Ἶρις, ιδος, acc. Ἶριν, voc. Ἶρι, Iris, messenger of the gods in the Iliad. To men she usually appears under the assumed form of some mortal.

ιροσ.g: Ἶρος (ϝῖρις): Irus, a nickname of Arnaeus the beggar, given to him by the suitors of Penelope, because he went on errands, Od. 18.5 follg.

ισ.g: ίς (ϝίς, cf. vis), acc. ἶνα, pl. ἶνες, dat. ίνεσι: (1) sinew, collectively, Il. 17.522, elsewhere pl.—(2) strength, force, literally and fig.; freq. with gen. as periphrasis for the person, κρατερὴ ίς Ὀδυσῆος, i. e. the mighty strong Odysseus himself, Il. 23.720 and Il. 21.356.

ισαζω.g: ίσάζω (ϝῖσος), part. ίσάζουσα, mid. aor. iter. ἰσάσκετο: make equal, balance, Il. 12.435; mid., deem oneself equal, vie with, Il. 24.607.

ισανδροσ.g: Ἴσανδρος : Isander, son of Bellerophon, slain by Ares, Il. 6.197, 203.

ισθμιον.g: ἴσθμιον : necklace, Od. 18.300†. (See cuts Nos. 2, 40, 41 and 93.)

ισκε.g: ἴσκε : defective ipf., perhaps from the same root as ἔσπετε, said, spoke, Od. 19.203, Od. 22.31.

ισμαροσ.g: Ἴσμαρος : a city of the Ciconians, Od. 9.40.

ισο-θεοσ.g: ίσό-θεος (ϝῖσος): equal to the gods, godlike; always ίσόθεος φῶς. (Il., and of Telemachus, Od. 1.324, Od. 20.124.)

ισο-μοροσ.g: ίσό-μορος (ϝῖσος): of equal lot, a peer, Il. 15.209†.

ισοσ.g: ἶσος (ϝῖσος, Att. ἴσος), ίση, ἶσον: equal in size, weight, or number, also like; freq. ίση as subst., μή τίς μοι ἀτεμβόμενος κίοι ίσης, of an equal share in the feast, Od. 9.42, Il. 11.705, Il. 12.423; also ἶσα as subst, ‘reparation,’ Od. 2.203. —Adv., ἶσον, ἶσα, equally, on equal terms, Il. 9.616; also κατὰ ϝῖσα, ἐπὶ ϝῖσα, ‘equally balanced,’ ‘undecided, Il. 11.336, Il. 12.436, Il. 15.413.

ισο-φαριζω.g: ίσο-φαρίζω (ϝῖσος, φέρω): deem oneself equal, vie with, rival, in anything (τὶ), Il. 6.101, Il. 9.390. (Il.）

ισο - φοροσ.g: ίσο - φόρος : bearing alike, equally strong, Od. 18.373†.

ισοω.g: ίσόω (ϝῖσος), mid. aor. opt. ίσωσαίμην: mid., compare oneself, Od. 7.212†.

ιστημι.g: ἵστημι , ἱστᾶσι, imp. ἵστη, inf. ἱστάμεναι, ipf. iter. ἵστασκε, 3 pl. ἵστασαν, fut. inf. στήσειν, aor. 1 ἔστησα, στῆσα, aor. 2 ἔστην, στῆν, 3 pl. ἔστησαν, ἔσταν, στάν, iter. στάσκε, subj. στήῃς, στήῃ, 1 pl. στέωμεν, στείομεν, perf. ἕστηκα, du. ἕστατον, 2 pl. ἕστητε, 3 pl. ἑστᾶσι, subj. ἑστήκῃ, imp. ἕσταθι, ἕστατε, inf. ἑστάμεν（αι), part. ἑσταότος, etc., also ἑστεῶτα, etc., plup. 1 pl. ἕσταμεν.—Mid. (and pass.), ἵσταμαι, imp. ἵστασο, ipf. ἵστατο, fut. στήσομαι, aor. 1 στήσαντο, στήσασθαι, -σάμενος, aor. pass. ἐστάθη: I. trans. (pres., ipf., fut., and aor. 1 act.), set in place, set on foot, cause to stand, rise, or stop; of marshalling soldiers, στίχας, λα_όν, Β 525, Il. 6.433; causing clouds, waves, to rise, Od. 12.405, Il. 21.313; bringing horses to a standstill, ships to anchor, Il. 5.368, Od. 3.182; metaph., ‘excite,’ ‘rouse,’ battle, strife, Od. 11.314, Od. 16.292; weigh, Il. 19.247, Il. 22.350, Il. 24.232.— Mid. aor. 1 is causative, set up or set on foot for oneself, or something of one's own, κρητῆρα, ἱστόν, met., μάχην, Ζ 528, Il. 1.480, Od. 9.54.—II. intrans. (pass., fut. mid., aor. 2 and perf. and plup. act.), place oneself, come to a stand, rise, perf. and plup., stand; κῦμα ἵσταται, Il. 21.240; ὀφθαλμοὶ ὡσεὶ κέρα_ ἕστασαν, ‘were fixed,’ Od. 19.211 ; στῆ δ᾽ ὀρθός, ὀρθαὶ τρίχες ἔσταν, Il. 24.359; met., νεῖκος ἵσταται, ἕβδομος ἑστήκει μείς, ‘had set in,’ Il. 19.117 ; μὴν ἱστάμενος, ‘beginning of the month,’ Od. 14.162, Od. 19.307; of spring, Od. 19.519; aor. pass., ὁ δ᾽ ἐστάθη ἠύτε πέτρη, Od. 17.463.

ιστιαια.g: Ἱστίαια : a city in Euboea, Il. 2.537†.

ιστιον.g: ἱστίον (ἱστός): sail. (See cut, from an ancient coin bearing the inscription ΝΙΚΟΜΗΔΙΩΝ. ΔΙΣ. ΝΕΩΚΟΡΩΝ.)

ιστο-δοκη.g: ἱστο-δόκη (δέχομαι): mast - receiver, mast-crutch, a saw-horse shaped support on the after-deck to receive the mast when lowered, Il. 1.434†. (Plate IV.)

ιστο-πεδη.g: ἱστο-πέδη : mast-stay, mast-block, a thwart or transverse beam with a depression into which the mast fitted, which was by this means, as well as by the ἐπίτονοι, prevented from falling forward, Od. 12.51. (See cut, letter b.)

ιστοσ.g: ίστός (ἵστημι): anything that stands. —(1) mast, in the middle of the ship, held in place by the μεσόδμη, ἱστοπέδη, πρότονοι, ἐπίτονοι. During stay in port the mast was unstepped and laid back upon the ἱστοδόκη (cf. preceding cut, and Nos. 60, 84).—(2) weaver's beam, loom. The frame of the loom was not placed, as in modern handlooms, in a horizontal position, but stood upright, as appears in the cut, representing an ancient Egyptian loom. The threads of the warp hung perpendicularly down, and were drawn tight by weights at their lower ends. To set up the beam and so begin the web is (ἱστὸν) στήσασθαι. In weaving, the weaver passed from one side to the other before the loom (ἐποίχεσθαι), as he carried the shuttle (κανών), on which was wound the thread of the woof, through the warp, and then drove the woof home with a blow of the κερκίς.— (3) warp, and in general, web, woven stuff.

ιστωρ.g: ἴστωρ , ορος (root ϝιδ): one who knows, judge, Il. 18.501, Il. 21.486.

ισχαναω, ισχανω.g: ἰσχανάω, ἰσχάνω (ἴσχω), ipf. iter. ἰσχανάασκον: hold, restrain, detain, Il. 17.747, Od. 15.346; intrans., w. gen., or inf., hold to, crave, desire, Il. 17.572, Il. 23.300, Od. 8.288; mid., restrain oneself, delay, Il. 12.38, Il. 19.234, Od. 7.161.

ισχιον.g: ἰσχίον (cf. ἰξύς): hip-joint, Il. 5.306; then the parts about the hips, loins, flanks.

ισχω.g: ἴσχω (σισέχω, root σεχ, ἔχω), inf. ἰσχέμεναι, mid. ipf. ἴσχετο: hold in the simplest sense, then hold back, check, restrain, τινός, ‘from’ something, Il. 5.90; mid., restrain oneself, stop, desist from (τινός), Od. 22.367, Od. 24.54.

ιτυλοσ.g: Ἴτυλος : Itylus (in the tragic poets Itus), son of Aēdon, slain by her through mistake, and lamented in her plaintive notes, of which the name is an imitation, Od. 19.522†.

ιτυμονευσ.g: Ἰτυμονεύς : son of Hypirochus in Elis, slain by Nestor, Il. 11.672†.

ιτων.g: Ἴτων : a town in Thessaly, Il. 2.696†.

ιυγμοσ.g: ίυγμός : cry of joy, jubilant outcry, Il. 18.572†.

ιυζω.g: ἰύζω : cry out, scream with intent to scare something away, Od. 15.162 and Il. 17.66.

ιφευσ.g: Ἰφεύς (ϝιφ.): a Trojan, slain by Patroclus, Il. 16.417†.

ιφθιμη.g: Ἰφθίμη : daughter of Icarius, the sister of Penelope and wife of Eumēlus, Od. 4.797†.

ιφθι_μοσ.g: ἴφθι_μος : doubtful word, mighty, strong, goodly, the latter interpretation to suit the epith. as applied to women, ἄλοχος, θυγάτηρ, Πηρώ, Il. 5.415, ο 364, Od. 11.287.

ιφι.g: ἶφι (ϝίς): with might, ἀνάσσειν, etc.; by violence, κτάμενος, Il. 3.375.

ιφιανασσα.g: Ἰφιάνασσα : Iphianassa, daughter of Agamemnon, Il. 9.145 and 287.

ιφιδαμασ.g: Ἰφιδάμας : son of Antēnor and Theāno, Il. 11.21 ff.

ιφικληειοσ.g: Ἰφικλήειος : of Iphiclus, βίη ?᾿ιφικληείη, i. e. the mighty Iphiclus himself (see βίη), Od. 11.290, 296.

ιφικλοσ.g: Ἴφικλος : son of Phylacus, father of Podarces and Protesilāüs, Il. 2.705, Il. 13.698, Il. 23.636, Od. 11.289 ff.

ιφιμεδεια.g: Ἰφιμέδεια : wife of Alōeus, and mother of Otus and Ephialtes, Od. 11.305.

ιφινοοσ.g: Ἰφίνοος : son of Dexius, slain by Glaucus, Il. 7.14†.

ιφιοσ.g: ίφιος : strong, fat, goodly, only ίφια μῆλα.

ιφισ.g: Ἶφις : from Scyros, a slave of Patroclus, Il. 9.667†.

ιφιτιδησ.g: Ἰφιτίδης : son of Iphitus, Archeptolemus, Il. 8.128†.

ιφιτιων.g: Ἰφιτίων : son of Otrynteus, slain by Achilles, Il. 20.382.

ιφιτοσ.g: Ἴφιτος (ϝιφ.): Iphitus.—(1) son of Eurytus, an Argonaut, guest-friend of Odysseus, slain by Heracles, Od. 21.14-37. —(2) son of Nautolus, an Argonaut, from Phocis, father of Schedius and Epistrophus, Il. 2.518, Il. 17.306.—(3) father of Archeptolemus.

ιχθυαω.g: ἰχθυάω , ipf. iter. ἰχθυάασκον: catch fish, fish, Od. 12.95 and Od. 4.368.

ιχθυοεισ.g: ἰχθυόεις , only -όεντι, -όεντα: abounding in fish, fishy.

ιχθυσ.g: ἰχθύς , ύος, acc. pl. ἰχθύας, ἰχθῦς: fish.

ιχνοσ.g: ἴχνος , εος: foot-step, track, trace, Od. 17.317†.

ιχωρ.g: ίχώρ , acc. ἰχῶ: ichor, attributed to the gods in place of blood, see Il. 5.339-342.

ιψ.g: ίψ , ίπός: worm that eats into horn or wood, borer, Od. 21.395.

ιωγη.g: ἰωγή : shelter; βορέω, ‘from’ the wind, Od. 14.533†. Cf. ἐπιωγαί.

ιωη.g: ἰωή : sound of a voice, Il. 10.139; tone of a lyre, Od. 17.261; whistling of the wind, Il. 4.276, Il. 11.308.

ιωκη.g: ἰωκή , acc. ἰῶκα (διώκω): pursuit, attack, battle - tumult. Personified, Il. 5.740. (Il.)
